newsitem.title: UK: Panamax rates continue slow improvement.
newsitem.headline: Panamax rates continue slow improvement.

text.p: A rise of seven points in the Baltic Freight Index on Thursday to 1017 (from a 9-year low of 992 in the middle of last week) reflected generally improved conditions for panamaxes, although owners' brokers conceded that squeezing rates upwards was a "slow grind".
Firmer coal fixtures from Newport News to Japan for end Oct and US Gulf/Japan grain for Nov 1/15 were reported together with steadier NoPac round voyage rates.
Some brokers believed that a good volume of grain business remains to be quoted from North America for end Oct/early Nov.
The continent continues firm for the smaller early handies, especially lakers, but at the the other end of the scale the market is still grim everywhere for capers.
GRAIN - Navix were reported to have fixed 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Nov 1/15 at $20.00 basis no combo which compares with last reported of $18.75/19.00 for Oct 15/25.

Although Tradigrain have fixed Chinese tonnage for 50,000 heavy grain USGulf/China for Oct 19/25 at only $17.75, brokers considered that the US Gulf mid-Oct position was proving increasingly difficult for charterers with business still unfixed.
Continental with a stem to Aqaba for shipment by Oct 13, Seatrans to Egypt by Oct 17, and Cobelfret to the Continent by Oct 25 were among those said to be in this category.
Klaveness quoted a new enquiry 60,000 hevy grain US Gulf/Antwerp-Hamburg for Oct 25/Nov 5.
Stem problems were rumoured in the firmer North Pacific area where Continental have had a Maersk Panamax on extended subjects for a trip to the far east.

Atlantic Savior 64,754 dwt was believed to have agreed delivery NoPac Oct 15/20 trip China with Chinese charterers at $7,200 daily plus $110,000 but still awaited confirmation of stem, and similar business at this rate was reported fixed also on subjects by Samsun Spirit 67,000 dwt.

Rani Padmini 76,384 dwt was believed fixed by Toepfer from Nopac to Saudi Arabia on private terms. Handy grain business included reports of Cargill booking Fassa for 32,600 barley from Norfolk to Jeddah at close to $23.00 and Dreyfus fixing on subjects 21,000 rapeseed La Pallice/Vera Cruz, both prompt. MINERALS - Capers continued to be fixed at unprofitable levels for owners. Cobelfret booked Nord-Power for 140,000 coal Richards Bay/Rotterdam for Nov 12/20 at $5.25, down 25 cents on last fixed.
Van Ommeren fixed 100,000 coal Baltimore/Redcar on subjects at $5.30 for Oct/Nov and Preag covered 100,000 Bolivar/Wilhelmshaven for early Nov on private terms.

Some brokers considered that the closure of Narvik will improve demand for capers with substitute supplies of ironore having to be shipped from more distant loading areas, but others believed the current weak rates may panic owners into covering end year positions prematurely at even more distressed levels.

By contrast in the panamax sector a firmer rate of $15.00 or $15.25 was agreed by Navios for Blessing for 57,500 coal Newport News/Japan for end Oct. China Joy 70,000 dwt was fixed on timecharter by Safmarine for coal from S.Africa to the Continent on private terms. HANDY-SIZES - Some much firmer rates were rumoured paid from the Continent for lakers and smaller geared bulkers, but details remained secret in many cases.

Hero 19,000 dwt was thought to have fixed from the Baltic via the Continent to the Med and a 20,000 tonne parcel of fertilizers was rumoured booked to the far east at a rate in the region of 20 pct higher than last done. Meanwhile demand from US Gulf, S.America and S.Africa has remained poor. In the far east CSAV fixed a 42,000 dwt vessel from Japan for 2 laden legs round voyage via Chile at an unremarkable $7,000 daily.
